name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about four points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Greg Stanton runs with a large financial advantage ($2.0M cash vs. $0.3M)
No outside spending against Stanton and no general-election polling
Prediction markets price Stanton near 94% to win
model.rationale: Stanton combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and a roughly four-to-one cash advantage over Zuhdi Jasser, with no outside opposition spending and markets pricing him near certain. With no polls available, fundamentals and money point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Stanton or a favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset would require an unusual shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton seeks a fourth term in a Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He has raised over $2.1 million and holds roughly $2.0 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000 with $342,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and prediction markets price his reelection chances near 94 percent.

No general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those factors all point the same direction, supporting a Safe Democratic rating with an expected margin near eighteen points, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated without polling.
